paper_metadata.title: Recovery of Cerebral Blood Flow Following Sports-Related Concussion

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a highly homogeneous sample of collegiate football athletes, which minimizes confounding by age, sex, and fitness levels. The recruitment source and inclusion/exclusion criteria are well-defined, and baseline characteristics are compared between groups.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 44 male student athletes were recruited from a National Collegiate Athletic Association Division I football team.
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined as NCAA Division I male football athletes.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Physicians trained in sports medicine diagnosed concussions at the time of injury independently of the study
items.reasoning: Recruitment was based on independent clinical diagnosis by sports medicine staff, reducing selection bias by the researchers.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between March 2012 and December 2013.
items.reasoning: The specific dates for the study period are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment

items.evidence_snippet: at a private research institute specializing in neuroimaging... recruited from a National Collegiate Athletic Association Division I football team.
items.reasoning: The setting (NCAA Division I team and neuroimaging institute) is clearly stated.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: All athletes reported no premorbid mood disorders, anxiety disorders, substance abuse, or alcohol abuse.
items.reasoning: Specific psychiatric exclusion criteria and the 'zero time' (time of injury) are described.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a notable dropout rate from T1 (n=17) to T3 (n=13), representing a 23.5% loss. While the authors used linear mixed-effects models to handle missing data, the reasons for dropout and the characteristics of those lost to follow-up are not detailed.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Seventeen concussed athletes were assessed... 15 athletes returned for a second visit... 13 athletes completing a final assessment
items.reasoning: Retention was 76% at 1 month. While acceptable for neuroimaging, it introduces some risk of attrition bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (CBF) was measured using standardized, objective neuroimaging (ASL-MRI). The methodology is technically rigorous and applied consistently across the sample.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Arterial spin labeling magnetic resonance imaging was used to collect voxelwise relative CBF at each visit.
items.reasoning: The prognostic factor (CBF) and the method (ASL-MRI) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Neuroimaging data were collected using a General Electric Discovery MR750 3-T MRI scanner... quantified to milliliters per 100 g per minute
items.reasoning: 3T MRI with ASL is a validated, objective method for measuring CBF.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: A relative CBF image was calculated by dividing the smoothed quantified CBF image by the average CBF value.
items.reasoning: CBF is treated as a continuous variable in the voxelwise and ROI analyses.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Neuroimaging data were collected using a General Electric Discovery MR750 3-T MRI scanner.
items.reasoning: All participants were scanned using the same equipment and protocol.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: All concussed athletes completed at least 2 of the 3 visits.
items.reasoning: While there was attrition, the majority of the sample provided longitudinal data.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: linear mixed-effects model analysis, with time as a fixed factor and a random intercept to account for missing data.
items.reasoning: Linear mixed-effects models are the standard and appropriate method for handling missing data in longitudinal studies.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a mix of objective (cognitive) and subjective (clinician-rated) outcomes. A significant risk is noted regarding the lack of blinding for the clinicians performing the neuropsychiatric assessments.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The number of days that athletes were withheld from competition following injury (ie, days until return-to-play decision) was used to stratify groups
items.reasoning: The primary outcome (Return to Play) and secondary outcomes (HAM-A/D) are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Alternatively, current results could be reflective of clinician rater bias (ie, nonblinded) in the assessment of postconcussive symptoms.
items.reasoning: The authors explicitly acknowledge that the clinicians were not blinded, which is a risk for the neuropsychiatric ratings.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Neuropsychiatric evaluations and a brief cognitive screen were also performed at all 3 points.
items.reasoning: Standardized batteries were used for all participants at all time points.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study design effectively controls for major confounders by using a control group of healthy athletes from the same team (matching for age, sex, and physical activity). Multivariable adjustment for concussion history was also performed.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured

items.evidence_snippet: Table 1. Player Position, Medication Status, and Demographic Information

items.reasoning: Concussion history and timing are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: concussed athletes to self-report more previously diagnosed concussions

items.evidence_snippet: Structured interviews... were collected at each visit
items.reasoning: Data collection was standardized across groups.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: linear mixed-effects model analysis... to account for missing data.
items.reasoning: The statistical model handles missingness in covariates/confounders appropriately.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: Cross-sectional validation was conducted against healthy football athletes to maximally control for nonspecific confounds
items.reasoning: The use of teammates as controls is an excellent design choice to control for lifestyle and fitness confounders.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: Supplemental analyses examined the effect of concussion history on CBF and neurobehavioral measures.
items.reasoning: The authors specifically tested if concussion history influenced the results.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is robust, using linear mixed-effects models and stringent Bonferroni corrections for multiple comparisons. The reporting is transparent regarding both significant and non-significant findings.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Statistical analyses were performed in Systat. Repeated-measure analyses were performed for each measure using a linear mixed-effects model
items.reasoning: The analytical plan is detailed and follows best practices for longitudinal data.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Longitudinal points were selected to mirror the typical recovery period from concussion reported in other large-scale cognitive and behavioral studies
items.reasoning: The model is based on established clinical recovery timelines.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: A conservative corrected significance level of P < .002 was considered following Bonferroni correction
items.reasoning: The use of mixed models and strict alpha-level corrections protects against Type I errors.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Correlations with other behavioral measures exhibiting a main effect of time were not significant (P > .10 for all).
items.reasoning: The authors report non-significant findings and exploratory results transparently.
